P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Receiving FX for exported services is allowed and largely unrestricted. (1) The NBU's export settlement deadline (180 days for transactions since 5 Apr 2022 under martial-law Resolution 18) does NOT apply to exports of works, services (except transport and insurance) and intellectual-property rights. This exemption has existed since NBU Resolution 67 of 14 May 2019, and tax practitioners confirmed it still applied in July 2026. (2) There is no mandatory sale of FX proceeds: the NBU abolished the surrender requirement from 20 June 2019. A sole proprietor (FOP) sells FX only on their own instruction. Other martial-law FX restrictions under Resolution 18, e.g. on purchasing FX and transfers abroad, still apply and were not researched here.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. FOPs receive client payments in a foreign-currency (валютний) account at a Ukrainian bank. Income is recognised at the NBU rate on the day the FX is credited, and later sale of the FX is the FOP's own choice. For single-tax group 3, FX gains on that sale are not taxable. Funds received on foreign bank accounts must be moved to the Ukrainian FX account within 180 days (practitioner guidance).

P4_paypal.answer: Yes. PayPal publishes a fee schedule for Ukraine (UA) residents covering buying, 'Selling with PayPal' (commercial transactions) and personal transfers. Withdrawing a personal-account balance to cards in UA carries no PayPal fee when no currency conversion is involved. Since March 2022 Ukrainians can receive P2P payments and withdraw to Ukrainian Visa and Mastercard cards. P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: widely used, and Etsy pays Ukrainian sellers via Payoneer (automated collector). The tax service's position is that for single-tax FOPs, funds received on Payoneer (and similar systems) count as single-tax income if moved to the FOP's Ukrainian bank account by the end of the reporting period (a quarter for group 3). Funds left abroad, or sent to a personal account, are taxed as an individual's foreign income (18% PIT plus military levy). Income date is the date credited to Payoneer. Wise: Ukraine is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money. Practitioner articles still mention Wise in the same tax rule, presumably for accounts opened elsewhere.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest form: an individual entrepreneur (ФОП, FOP). State registration is free and can be done automatically in Diia, with the application taking about 10 minutes. Applicants choose the tax system and KVED codes, and a group-3 single taxpayer is entered in the register within 2 working days. Requirements are Ukrainian citizenship, an assigned taxpayer number (РНОКПП) and a qualified e-signature (Diia.Pidpys). FOP status is in practice needed for local acquiring (P3) and for the single-tax treatment of foreign income (P5, L3).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Individuals use the РНОКПП (registration number of the taxpayer's account card, formerly 'identification number'). It is assigned by the State Tax Service on submission of form 1DR with an identity document, in person, by post or through the online e-cabinet (cabinet.tax.gov.ua). L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents, including registered freelancers and entrepreneurs, are taxed on worldwide income. Foreign income of individuals: 18% PIT plus military levy of 5% (raised from 1.5% from 1 Dec 2024, Law 4015-IX). Simplified (single-tax) group 3, the usual regime for IT and digital service FOPs: 5% of revenue (non-VAT payer) or 3% (VAT payer), plus military levy of 1% of revenue, plus minimum social contribution (ЄСВ) of UAH 1,902.34/month in 2026. The 2026 income cap is 1,167 minimum wages = UAH 10,091,049.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT is 20% (reduced 14% and 7%; 0% for goods exports). Compulsory registration once taxable supplies exceed UAH 1 million over the past 12 months; voluntary registration earlier. Exported services: consulting, engineering, legal and the other services listed in Tax Code art. 186.3(в) are supplied where the recipient is registered. When supplied to a non-resident they are outside Ukraine's VAT scope (no VAT, no input recovery). A non-VAT-registered provider charges no VAT anyway. Group-3 FOPs at 5% are non-VAT payers.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 'On Personal Data Protection' No. 2297-VI (in force since 2011) applies, supervised by the Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights (Ombudsman). There is no general database registration. Controllers notify the Ombudsman ONLY about processing that poses a special risk (sensitive data, e.g. health, biometrics, ethnicity, criminal records), within 30 working days of starting it. Processing generally needs consent unless the law provides another ground. A GDPR-style replacement (draft law 8153) passed first reading but was not enacted as of 2026.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: The 1991 Law 'On Consumer Rights Protection' (No. 1023-XII), art. 13, still applies to distance contracts. The consumer may terminate within 14 days of the information confirmation or of receiving the goods, extended to 90 days if the confirmation is missing or defective. There is no right to terminate where, with the consumer's consent, a service or goods were delivered electronically before the period ended and the consumer was told so. The new consumer law No. 3153-IX (14-day withdrawal with digital-content rules) enters into force one year after publication but NOT before martial law ends. Martial law was extended to 31 Oct 2026, so the old law remains in force.

L7_incentives.answer: (1) Single-tax group 3: 5% of revenue plus 1% military levy instead of 18% PIT plus 5% levy, with simplified reporting and no VAT if non-registered, up to UAH 10.09m (2026). D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The passport of a citizen of Ukraine as an ID card (biometric) or, for older holders, the 1994 booklet passport, plus the biometric foreign-travel passport. Diia shows digital ID cards and biometric passports with the same legal force as the plastic ones, usable for banking services. 1994 booklets and old-style foreign passports are not shown in Diia. W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed). The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
